subject: english-literature
title: Context and Comparison
welcome_lead: Even with an unseen poem, you bring context. And many exam tasks ask comparison. Master both moves.
meta_desc: Contextualising unseen poetry and comparative tasks at A-Level English Literature.
final_note: You can now situate the unseen poem in tradition and pair it with another for confident comparison.

concepts.def: Wordsworth and Coleridge revolution; 'language really used by men'; preface to 1800 edition manifesto.
Burke 1757 distinguished sublime (terror, vastness) from beautiful (delicacy); central to Romantic aesthetic.
Innocence's dark counterpart; 'Tyger' and 'London'; critique of institutional oppression.
Wonder year: Nightingale, Grecian Urn, Autumn, Melancholy, Psyche; 'negative capability' theory.
Poets as 'unacknowledged legislators of the world'; visionary politics; published posthumously 1840.
Autobiographical epic in blank verse; spots of time; growth of poet's mind; 1805 and 1850 versions.

walkthroughs.body_html:
A poem about trenches, gas and barbed wire situates itself in the First World War without naming dates.

Always justify contextual claims with textual evidence.
For comparison, decide the axis. Same theme, different mode? Same form, different politics? Begin with the axis and let details follow.
Owen's Dulce et Decorum Est and Brooke's The Soldier share the war theme but oppose it tonally. The contrast becomes the essay.

numericals.q: In what year were Keats's great odes written?

free_texts.q: Name Keats's concept of openness to mystery.
free_texts.hint: Two words; from letter to brothers 1817.
